examples.en: They caught the criminal thanks to a citizen's tip.
Many tips came in to the TV station.

examples.ko: 저는 이상한 일을 보고 바로 제보를 했어요.
examples.en: I saw something strange and reported it right away.
They take news tips by phone or email.
It was an anonymous tip, so I do not know who sent it.

examples.ko: 제보 덕분에 사고 원인을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the tip, we learned the cause of the accident.

explain: '제보'는 뉴스, 경찰, 회사 같은 곳에 사건이나 정보를 알려 주는 일이에요. 친구에게 알려 주는 것은 '알려 주다'이고, '제보'는 공적인 곳에 보내는 느낌이에요. 보통 '제보를 받다', '제보가 들어오다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The police received a tip from a citizen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알려 주는 정보를 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pair, from the side receiving the information.

phrases.en: The informant's name is secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보를 알려 준 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who gave the information.

phrases.en: I made a tip-off call to the TV station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이나 정보를 알리려고 거는 전화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phone call made to report an event or information.

explain_en: 제보 is telling news, police or a company about an incident or information. Telling a friend is 알려 주다, while 제보 is directed to an official place. It often goes with 제보를 받다 or 제보가 들어오다.

examples.ko: 도로에 큰 구멍이 있어서 시청에 제보했어요.
examples.en: There was a big hole in the road, so I reported it to city hall.

examples.ko: 사고를 본 사람은 경찰에 제보해 주세요.
examples.en: If you saw the accident, please tell the police.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 몰래 버리는 사람을 구청에 제보할 거예요.
examples.en: I will report the person secretly dumping trash to the district office.
Please tell me how to send a tip to the TV station.

examples.ko: 직원이 회사의 문제를 기자에게 제보한 일이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a case where an employee tipped a reporter about the company's problem.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 위험한 일을 보면 시청에 제보하세요.
examples.en: If you see something dangerous at a construction site, report it to the city hall.

explain: '제보하다'는 경찰, 방송국, 구청처럼 공적인 곳에 알리는 말이에요. 개인에게 알릴 때는 '알려 주다'를 쓰고, 나쁜 일을 알릴 때는 '신고하다'가 더 가까워요. '신고하다'는 법적으로 알리는 느낌이고 '제보하다'는 정보를 준다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I tipped off the police about the accident site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 알렸다는 말로, 신고한 일을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, used when talking about something you reported.

phrases.en: If you report a problem, the district office checks it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알린 뒤에 어떤 일이 생기는지 조건으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what happens after you report something.

phrases.en: I'll report what I saw to the TV station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 알리겠다고 말할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you will report something.

explain_en: 제보하다 is telling a public place such as the police, a TV station or a district office. For a person you use 알려 주다, and for reporting wrongdoing 신고하다 is closer. 신고하다 feels legal, while 제보하다 is about giving information.

examples.en: The party leadership announced its position today.
The new leadership is made up of young people.
The student council leadership started talking with the school.
Everyone agreed to follow the leadership's decision.
The union leaders and the company met again.
Some suggested changing the leadership.

explain: 지도부는 정당, 노조, 학생회처럼 조직을 이끄는 사람들 전체를 말해요. 한 사람은 '지도자', 회사에서는 '경영진'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서 '당 지도부'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The union leadership met with the company's CEO.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노동조합을 이끄는 사람들 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for all the people who lead a labor union.

phrases.en: The leadership was replaced after the election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직을 이끄는 사람들이 새로 바뀔 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the people leading an organization are replaced.

phrases.en: The management announced a new plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정당이나 노조가 아니라 회사를 이끄는 사람들은 '경영진'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people who lead a company, not a party or union, use 경영진.

explain_en: The body of leaders of an organization, a group not a trait. 지도부 refers to the whole group of people leading an organization such as a party, union or student council. One person is a 지도자 (leader), and in companies the group is called 경영진 (management). The news often says '당 지도부' (party leadership).

en: to be passed; to go through

examples.en: My proposal was approved in the meeting.
That law has to be passed in the National Assembly.
If the document screening is passed, you'll get a call.
We only sell products that have passed inspection.

examples.ko: 계획서가 통과되지 않아서 다시 써야 해요.
examples.en: The plan wasn't approved, so I have to rewrite it.
I'm waiting until my application is approved.

explain: 심사, 검사, 투표 같은 단계를 무사히 넘어 인정받았다는 뜻이에요. 내가 시험에 붙을 때는 '통과하다'나 '합격하다'를 써요. 통과되다는 안건이나 서류처럼 사물이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My documents didn't pass the review.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심사를 넘지 못했다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it did not get past the review.

phrases.en: Please check the proposal that was passed yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I'm relieved the inspection passed without trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 없이 넘었을 때 '무사히'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 무사히 when something got through without problems.

explain_en: It means getting through a review, inspection, or vote and being accepted. When you yourself pass an exam, use 통과하다 or 합격하다. 통과되다 is natural when the subject is a thing like a proposal or document.

t90.ax: My proposal was approved in the meeting.

examples.en: The police called in the suspect yesterday and questioned him.
The suspect said from the start that he had done nothing wrong.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 피의자 얼굴은 보여 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: The news did not show the suspect's face.

examples.ko: 변호사가 피의자와 두 시간 동안 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The lawyer talked with the suspect for two hours.
The suspect in the case was caught last night.
The suspect's family cried in front of the reporters.

explain: 피의자는 경찰이나 검찰이 조사하는 단계의 사람이고, 재판에 넘겨지면 '피고인'이라고 불러요. 뉴스에서는 자주 들리지만 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: There will be a suspect interrogation at the police station tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 덩어리 표현으로, 경찰이 조사하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common set phrase in the news for the police questioning a suspect.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 사고 때문에 피의자로 조사받았어요.
phrases.en: He was investigated as a suspect because of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로 조사받다'를 붙여 어떤 신분으로 조사받는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-로 조사받다' tells in what status someone is being investigated.
phrases.en_equiv: to be questioned as a suspect

phrases.en: He went to the police station as a suspect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건에서 그 사람의 법적인 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's legal position in a case.

explain_en: Legal term, person officially under investigation (police, news) 피의자 is the person under investigation by police or prosecutors; once the case goes to trial the person is called 피고인. You hear it often in the news but almost never in everyday talk.

t90.ax: The news did not show the suspect's face.

en: to begin a class; to begin a course

examples.en: Universities start the semester in early March.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 영어 수업이 개강해서 바빠요.
examples.en: The English course starts next week, so I am busy.
The new class at the academy started on Monday.
I bought the textbook before the course started.

examples.ko: 방학이 끝나고 개강할 때가 되니 아쉬워요.
examples.en: Now that the break is over and school is about to start, I feel sad.
I heard the semester starts in the first week of September.

explain: 학교나 학원에서 새 학기나 새 강좌가 시작될 때 써요. 반대로 학기가 끝나는 것은 '종강하다'예요. 학생들은 '개강 첫날'처럼 명사로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: There was a lot of homework from the first day of the semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사로 학기 시작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun form to talk about the start of a term.

phrases.en: When is the start date of classes?
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 시작되는 날을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask when classes begin.

phrases.example: 친구들을 만날 수 있어서 개강을 기다려요.
phrases.en: I am looking forward to the semester because I can meet my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학기 시작을 기대할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking forward to a term starting.
phrases.en_equiv: to look forward to the start of class

explain_en: It is used when a new semester or course begins at a school or academy. The opposite, the end of a term, is '종강하다'. Students also use the noun form, as in '개강 첫날'.

examples.en: An economist appeared on the news and explained prices.
My uncle is an economist who works at a university.
Economists carefully predict next year's economy.
I want to become an economist someday.

examples.ko: 경제학자의 책을 읽고 돈에 대해 많이 배웠어요.
examples.en: I read an economist's book and learned a lot about money.
Each economist thinks differently about this opinion.

explain: '경제학자'는 경제를 연구하는 학자예요. 은행이나 회사에서 시장을 살피는 사람은 '이코노미스트'나 '분석가'라고 부르기도 해요. 뉴스에서 '유명 경제학자'처럼 이름 앞에 자주 붙어요.

phrases.en: A famous economist gave a lecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 강연 소식에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in news and lecture announcements.

phrases.en: I want to become an economist when I grow up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about dreams or careers.

phrases.example: 경제학자의 말에 따르면 물가가 오를 거예요.
phrases.en: According to the economist, prices will rise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의 말에 따르면'은 전문가의 설명을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '의 말에 따르면' is used to report what an expert said.

explain_en: 경제학자 is a scholar who studies the economy. People who watch markets at banks or companies are sometimes called 이코노미스트 or 분석가. On the news you often see it before a name, as in 유명 경제학자.

examples.en: At Lunar New Year I go down to my hometown.
My grandmother still celebrates the Lunar New Year.
The highway is jammed during the Lunar New Year holiday.

examples.ko: 구정은 해마다 일월 말이나 이월에 있어요.
examples.en: Lunar New Year falls in late January or February each year.
When Lunar New Year comes, we eat tteokguk.
I got New Year's money at Lunar New Year.

explain: 음력 1월 1일을 부르던 옛 이름이에요. 지금은 공식 이름이 '설날'이고, 양력 1월 1일은 '신정'이에요. 어른들은 아직 '구정'이라고 많이 부르지만 젊은 사람들은 '설'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: These days, we eat rice cake soup with family on Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구정'보다 지금 공식적으로 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name used today, instead of '구정'.

phrases.en: All the relatives gather at Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '때'를 붙이면 그 기간쯤을 가리키는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '때' refers to that period of time.

phrases.en: Sinjeong is January 1 on the solar calendar, and Gujeong is January 1 on the lunar calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구정'과 짝이 되는 말로, 양력 새해 첫날이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of '구정': New Year's Day on the solar calendar.

explain_en: Old term for Lunar New Year (설날), spoken. It is the old name for the first day of the lunar calendar. The official name now is 설날, and January 1 on the regular calendar is 신정. Older people still often say 구정, while younger people say 설.

examples.en: The presidential press corps gathered at the briefing room.
The manager shared his thoughts in front of the press corps.
I applied to the school newspaper's reporter team.

examples.ko: 현장을 취재하려고 기자단은 아침 일찍 출발했어요.
examples.en: The press group left early in the morning to cover the scene.

examples.ko: 청소년 기자단 활동을 하면서 글쓰기를 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned writing through youth reporter activities.
This company recruits a blogger reporter team.

explain: '기자단'은 정부나 기관을 함께 취재하는 기자들의 모임이에요. 학교나 회사에서는 글을 쓰며 알리는 학생이나 시민 모임도 '기자단'이라고 불러요. '기자들'은 그냥 여러 명이고 '기자단'은 하나의 조직이라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: I joined the school press group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임의 한 사람이 된다는 뜻으로 '가입하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '가입하다' to mean becoming a member of the group.

phrases.en: The mayor meets the press corps this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기자들이 모인 조직과 만나 이야기한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means meeting and talking with the organized group of reporters.

phrases.en: The student reporters write the school news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생들이 모여 글을 쓰며 알리는 모임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a group of students who write and report news.

explain_en: 기자단 is a group of reporters who cover a government or organization together. Schools and companies also call a group of students or citizens who write and publicize things a 기자단. 기자들 just means several reporters, while 기자단 is one organization.

en: to act silly; to fool around

examples.en: My little brother keeps fooling around and it's chaotic.
You must not act silly in front of the teacher.
I was fooling around too much and broke a cup.
Stop messing around and sit quietly!

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 산책할 때 제일 많이 까불어요.
examples.en: My puppy acts the silliest when we go for walks.

examples.ko: 형이 아직도 애처럼 까부는 게 웃겨요.
examples.en: It's funny that my brother still acts like a kid.

explain: 까불다는 가볍고 시끄럽게 장난치는 모습이에요. 아이나 강아지에게는 귀엽게 들리지만 어른에게 '까불지 마'라고 하면 건방지다는 경고라서 아주 세게 들려요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '까부는, 까부세요'처럼 활용해요.

phrases.en: The classroom is noisy because of the kids fooling around.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㄹ이 빠진 활용형으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form with ㄹ dropped, modifying the noun after it.

phrases.en: Please don't fool around here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 말할 때 써요. 반말 '까불지 마'는 아주 세게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tells someone to stop. The casual 까불지 마 sounds very harsh.

phrases.en: Stop fooling around and sit down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 다음에 할 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -고 to link to what to do next.

explain_en: 까불다 describes noisy, light-hearted messing around. It sounds cute for a child or puppy, but telling an adult 까불지 마 is a harsh warning meaning "don't get cocky." The ㄹ drops before some endings, as in 까부는 and 까부세요.

examples.en: The baby is eating happily, yum-yum.
Yum-yum, this cake is really delicious!
The puppy is munching on its treat.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 냠냠 소리를 내면서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: My daughter makes yum-yum sounds while eating.
After eating it all up, I'm full.

examples.ko: 자, 이제 우리 같이 냠냠 해 볼까요?
examples.en: Now, shall we dig in together?

explain: 아이에게 '냠냠 먹자'처럼 말하거나 동화, 아기 말투에서 써요. 어른끼리 진지한 자리에서는 잘 안 써요. '쩝쩝'은 입 소리가 시끄럽다는 느낌이라 칭찬이 아니에요.

phrases.en: I said "Let's eat yum-yum!" to the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이에게 같이 먹자고 할 때 쓰는 귀여운 반말 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute casual-speech way to invite a child to eat together.

phrases.en: The child eats bread happily, yum-yum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛있게 먹는 소리와 모습을 함께 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows both the sound and the look of eating happily.

phrases.en: I eat slowly and enjoy my food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냠냠'을 쓰지 않는 어른끼리의 말로, 어디서나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral version without '냠냠' that works for adults anywhere.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat well, enjoy a meal

explain_en: It is used when talking to children ('냠냠 먹자'), in picture books and baby talk, but rarely between adults in a serious setting. 쩝쩝 is a smacking noise and is not a compliment.

examples.ko: 병원에서 엑스레이를 찍으면 방사선이 아주 조금 나와요.
examples.en: When you take an X-ray at the hospital, a very small amount of radiation is emitted.

examples.ko: 방사선 치료를 받는 환자들이 이쪽에서 기다려요.
examples.en: Patients receiving radiation therapy wait over here.

examples.ko: 방사선을 막기 위해 납 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: They wear lead clothing to block radiation.

examples.ko: 우주 비행사는 강한 방사선에 노출될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Astronauts can be exposed to strong radiation.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤에 방사선 수치를 계속 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: After the accident, they keep checking the radiation levels.

examples.ko: 방사선은 눈에 보이지 않아서 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Radiation can't be seen, so you have to be more careful.

explain: 병원, 원자력, 우주 이야기에서 나와요. 비슷한 '방사능'은 방사선을 내는 능력이나 물질을 가리켜서 뉴스에서 '방사능 유출'이라고 해요. 방사선은 나오는 빛이나 입자 자체예요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 병원에서 방사선 치료를 받고 계세요.
phrases.en: My grandmother is receiving radiation treatment at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 방사선으로 병을 치료하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to treating disease with radiation at a hospital.

phrases.en: The radiation exam is over in a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엑스레이 같은 검사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for exams such as X-rays.

phrases.en: This machine gives off radiation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 물질에서 방사선이 밖으로 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means radiation comes out of a machine or substance.

explain_en: It appears in talk about hospitals, nuclear power, and space. The similar 방사능 refers to the ability or material that gives off radiation, as in the news phrase '방사능 유출' (radioactive leak). 방사선 is the emitted rays or particles themselves.

examples.en: My grandfather has trouble walking.

examples.ko: 이 길은 보행 전용이라서 차가 못 들어와요.
examples.en: This road is for pedestrians only, so cars can't enter.
Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.

examples.ko: 무릎을 다쳐서 보행 연습을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I hurt my knee, so I'm practicing walking.
Pedestrians must follow the signal.
Wait until the walk signal changes.

explain: '걷기'와 비슷하지만 안내문, 교통, 의료처럼 딱딱한 자리에서 써요. '보행자'(걷는 사람), '보행 신호'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요. 운동으로 걷는 건 '걷기'나 '산책'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Pedestrians must follow the traffic signal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 걷는 사람을 말하고 교통 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person walking on the road; common in traffic contexts.

phrases.en: Cross when the pedestrian signal turns green.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 길을 건너는 신호를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The signal that tells people when to cross the road.

phrases.en: Please don't look at your phone while walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 '걷는 동안'을 짧게 쓸 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on signs as a short way of saying 'while walking'.

explain_en: Formal term for walking in pedestrian or safety contexts. It is close to 걷기 but belongs in formal settings such as signage, traffic, and medicine. It shows up in 보행자 (pedestrian) and 보행 신호 (walk signal). Walking for exercise is called 걷기 or 산책.

examples.en: The cold wind blew and I shivered.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 그가 부르르 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, he suddenly flared up in anger.
My phone buzzed, so I opened my bag.
The water for the ramen is bubbling up.

examples.ko: 아이가 차가운 물에 닿자 부르르 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: The child touched cold water and gave a shiver.
I suddenly got goosebumps and shuddered.

explain: 몸이 짧게 한 번 떨리거나 물건이 진동하는 모양, 물이 확 끓는 모양, 갑자기 성을 내는 모양에 써요. '부들부들'은 계속 떨리는 느낌이고 '부르르'는 짧고 갑작스러운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I got into the cold water and shuddered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 한 번 떠는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 계속 떠는 '부들부들'과 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a short, single shudder, unlike the continuous shaking of 부들부들.

phrases.en: The water is boiling up fast in the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 갑자기 확 끓어오르는 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water suddenly coming to a rolling boil.

phrases.en: My phone vibrated during the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰 진동처럼 물건이 짧게 떨리는 소리와 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an object, like a phone on vibrate, shaking briefly.

explain_en: One sudden shudder, as from a chill or fright. It covers a quick shiver of the body, something vibrating, water suddenly boiling up, and a sudden flare of temper. '부들부들' feels like trembling that keeps going, while '부르르' is short and sudden.

t90.ax: The cold wind blew and I shivered.
